title: Aging‐Induced Ductile‐Brittle‐Ductile Transition in High‐Entropy Alloys and its Implications

recollection.starting_material: (Guess) Likely a multi-principal-element high-entropy alloy, such as equiatomic or near-equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn or a derivative thereof.
recollection.intervention: (Guess) The study might have subjected the alloy to different aging treatments at various temperatures/times to precipitate secondary phases and investigate their influence on mechanical behavior.
recollection.structure: (Guess) The resulting microstructure probably involved the formation of secondary phases (e.g., nanoprecipitates) and possibly the transformation of the face-centered cubic matrix into multiple phases contributing to changing ductility and brittleness.
recollection.mechanism: (Guess) The transition in ductile–brittle–ductile behavior might relate to precipitation-driven changes in slip characteristics, grain boundary cohesion, or coarsening of precipitates, altering how dislocations move and cracks propagate.
recollection.results: (Guess) The paper likely reported a critical aging regime where the alloy exhibited a severe drop in ductility (brittle regime), then regained ductility after further aging. Quantitatively, they may have discussed yield strength, tensile strength, and elongation values showing a dip and subsequent recovery.

score.note: The recollection generically identifies varied aging treatments and a ductile–brittle–ductile response, but misses the specific 600°C embrittlement and 750°C recovery treatments. Its structural and mechanistic claims are speculative and omit enhanced L12 ordering, jagged B2/FCC boundaries, elevated APBE/modulus, restricted cross-slip, and ductile boundary transition zones. No quantitative values are provided.
